messages.subject: problem with a binary factor with a single indicator, WARNING: could not compute standard errors!
parts:
Hi

I'm using lavaan for an SEM model with a binary dependent variable (Behavior), 5 latent factors (Self-efficacy, fear of dental care, perceived benefit, perceived barrier, and SES(soci-eco)). The fitted model was

full.model <- '
barriers=~K1+K2+K3+K5+K6+K7+k8+K9+K10
benefit=~W1+W2+W3+W4+W5+W6+W7+W8
dent.care=~S1+S2+S3+S4+S5+S6
self.eficacy=~Z1+Z2+Z3+Z4+Z5+Z6+Z7+Z8+Z9+Z10
ses=~incomefamilies + mothereducation + fathereducation

behavior =~ Behavior # behavior is a new defined LV, serving as my new response var. 
Behavior~~0*Behavior

# Regression models
behavior ~ a*barriers + b*dent.care+ f*self.eficacy + d*benefit + K*sex + L*teehtdisease + M*ses
self.eficacy ~ sf1*sex+ sf2*teehtdisease+sf3*ses
f.care ~  fs1*sex+ fs2*teehtdisease+fs3*ses 

# Mediator effect
benefit~c*barriers

# covariance effect
benefit ~~ self.eficacy
barriers ~~ self.eficacy
barriers  ~~  dent.care
benefit ~~ dent.care
self.eficacy ~~ dent.care
'

here you can find its diagram 

https://www.dropbox.com/s/1t39hdm1qrtmfrc/SEM-Dia.emf?dl=0

in running above model, I got below warnings.

Warning messages:
1: In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING: could not compute standard errors!
  lavaan NOTE: this may be a symptom that the model is not identified.

2: In lavaan::lavaan(model = full.model, data = dent, std.lv = T, missing = "listwise",  :
  lavaan WARNING: some estimated variances are negative
3: In lavaan::lavaan(model = full.model, data = dent, std.lv = T, missing = "listwise",  :
  lavaan WARNING: observed variable error term matrix (theta) is not positive definite; use inspect(fit,"theta") to investigate.


Warnings disappear if I remove 

behavior =~ Behavior  
Behavior~~0*Behavior

and in regression models replace new defined LV, behavior, with Behavior

I used these codes to overcome an issue discussed in below topic while ago.

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/lavaan/binary£16.39dependent£16.39variables%7Csort:relevance/lavaan/YFSL69umWx4/ZDVa2QgiAQAJ

Will appreciate if anyone could give an advise on how to tackle above lavaan WARNINGs a direct me to a right direction.

Regards,

parts: Are you using the lavaan function? What if you use the sem function (in the lavaan package) instead? I notice that you are not explicitly setting reference variables (fixing loading to 1 for one indicator per factor). What if you explicitly fix the loading for Behavior to 1, just as you fix the residual variance to 0?

parts:
Thanks for your reply. I'm using SEM function;

full.model.fit <- sem(full.model, data=dent,estimator="WLSMV", missing="listwise", std.lv = T, ordered="Behaviour")

I think using std.lv = T will set for each factor the loading of one observed indicator to 1. Am I right or I still need to fix the loading of a indicator to 1 manually for each factor?

I set loading of Behavior to 1. That is I replaced 

behavior =~ Behavior  
Behavior~~0*Behavior

to 

behavior =~ Behavior  
Behavior~~1*Behavior

The negative error disappeared but below warnings emerged

Warning messages:
1: In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING: could not compute standard errors!
  lavaan NOTE: this may be a symptom that the model is not identified.

2: In lav_model_test(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavpartable = lavpartable,  :
  lavaan WARNING: could not compute scaled test statistic

------------------------------------------
next time, I replaced

behavior =~ Behavior  
Behavior~~0*Behavior

to 

behavior =~ 1*Behavior  

I got below error;

Warning message:
In lav_object_post_check(lavobject) :
lavaan WARNING: some estimated variances are negative

messages.subject: Re: problem with a binary factor with a single indicator, WARNING: could not compute standard errors!
parts:
Ali--
Yes, using the sem function will impose the needed constraints.
However, your syntax does two different things. The first syntax:

behavior =~ Behavior  
Behavior~~0*Behavior

sets the residual variance of the observed variable to 0, while the second form

behavior =~ 1*Behavior 

sets the loading to 1. These are not the same thing. Still, the defaults of the sem function should do both. I don't know the source of your error message.
